Links: [{"title":"Row Level Security","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security"},{"title":"Securing your API","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api"},{"title":"Securing your data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/secure-data"},{"title":"RAG with Permissions","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/rag-with-permissions"},{"title":"Tables and data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/tables"},{"title":"Database","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview"},{"title":"Introducing: Postgres Best Practices","url":"https://supabase.com/blog/postgres-best-practices-for-ai-agents"},{"title":"API keys","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys"},{"title":"Realtime Authorization","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/authorization"},{"title":"Production Checklist","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod"}]

The Supabase RLS guide is at supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security. It's split into three parts: understanding RLS, securing a table with RLS, and an RLS reference for policy helper functions and patterns.

Key points from the search results:

- **Grants and policies:** Postgres checks grants first, which decide whether a role can run an operation at all. Policies then decide which rows that operation can reach. A missing grant fails with a 42501 error before any policy runs (index 1-16 to 1-18, 1-26).
- **Default grants:** Newer projects may still grant anon and authenticated full privileges on new public tables. Adding policies doesn't remove those grants, so the guide says to revoke them (index 1-7, 1-8).
- **Per-operation policies:** Write separate policies for select, insert, and update, and use `to` to name the role. Insert policies use `with check`, and an update needs a matching select policy (index 1-59, 1-70, 1-79).
- **Indexes:** Index any column your policies filter on, since an unindexed filter can turn a read into a sequential scan (index 1-81).
- **Views:** Views bypass RLS by default. On Postgres 15+, setting `security_invoker = true` makes a view respect the underlying table's policies (index 1-32, 1-87).
- **Testing:** The guide's workflow ends with a test file under `supabase/tests/` and running `supabase test db` (index 1-41, 1-43).

Related pages from the same search:

- **API keys:** Publishable keys resolve to the anon or authenticated role, while secret keys use service_role and bypass RLS. Keep secret keys server-side (index 8-11, 8-12).
- **Securing your API:** Grants and RLS are two separate layers, and both should be used for every exposed object (index 2-13).


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.
